statement: An id with an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate is refused where it enters CoSec, so two different ids never share a stored key: a Redis key is UTF-8, which writes the surrogate as `?`, and tenant `beta\uD800` would read the documents, memberships and revocations of tenant `beta?`. A token that claims one in its subject, tenant, jti, roles or policies is invalid (401 token-invalid) before any revocation is read, and CoSec's token issuer refuses to sign one; a forwarded identity naming one is malformed (400); a control request holding one in its path, query or body is 400; an authenticator, an API key record or a membership provider that gives one has failed (503); cosec-migrate rejects a converted document that holds one (INVALID_ID), and publishes nothing. A surrogate pair is a character like any other. A rate limit key value with one counts in an escaped bucket of its own, never in another value's.
guards: model:IdentifiersTest#well formed is what survives UTF-8
runtime:UnpairedSurrogatePipelineTest#an authenticator whose principal holds an unpaired surrogate is unavailable
runtime:UnpairedSurrogatePipelineTest#a membership provider whose answer holds an unpaired surrogate is unavailable
document:IdentityCodecTest#an id with an unpaired surrogate is refused as malformed
control:ControlHttpTest#a request holding an unpaired surrogate is a 400, wherever it holds it
engine:RateLimitObligationTest#a key value with an unpaired surrogate counts in a well formed bucket of its own
model:ScopeResolverTest#a declared app that cannot be an app id is rejected with or without a host app
migrate:ConverterTest#an id with an unpaired surrogate is rejected, and nothing is converted
